2026-08-05T12:58:22.4739051Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4744723Z 
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4745120Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4746402Z 
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4746889Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4747482Z 
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4749392Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4751493Z >
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4754290Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4757487Z >
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4758389Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4759303Z 
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4759482Z ### How to Use
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4759728Z 
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4760515Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4761364Z 
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4761536Z ```bash
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4762089Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4762887Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4763553Z ```
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4763761Z 
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4764032Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4764593Z ```bash
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4765169Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4766263Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4767232Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4768066Z ```
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4768269Z 
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4768976Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4769964Z ```bash
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4770559Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4771310Z ```
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4771517Z 
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4771853Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4772627Z ```bash
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4773194Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4774189Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4774974Z ```
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4775173Z 
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4775457Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4776138Z 
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4777874Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4779829Z 
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4779996Z ```bash
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4780449Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4781403Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4782330Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4782667Z 
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4783187Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4784338Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4785246Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4785740Z ```
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4786129Z 
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4787018Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4788105Z 
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4788275Z ```bash
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4789003Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4790000Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4790780Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4791265Z 
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4791721Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4792649Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4793239Z ```
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4793443Z 
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4793654Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4794539Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4795653Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4796961Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4798130Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4799336Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4799961Z 
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4800131Z ### Notes
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4800355Z 
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4801085Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4802760Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4804234Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4805698Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4807295Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4808564Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4809673Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-08-05T12:58:22.4810443Z </mcp-clis>
